statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is the maximum of the set { points[i][1] + points[j][1] + |points[i][0] - points[j][0]| | 0 <= i < j < n and |points[i][0] - points[j][0]| <= k }. Equivalently, for every such pair the candidate value is at most r, and there exists such a pair whose candidate value is exactly r.
preconditions: Let n = len(points). 2 <= n <= 100000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, len(points[i]) = 2, and points[i][0] and points[i][1] are integers in the closed interval [-100000000, 100000000]. For every 0 <= i < j < n, points[i][0] < points[j][0]. 0 <= k <= 200000000. There exist indices i,j with 0 <= i < j < n and |points[i][0] - points[j][0]| <= k.
